newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Spanish "mobile phone" hijacker freed in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Spanish "mobile phone" hijacker freed in Geneva.

text.p: A Geneva court ruled on Friday that a Spanish hijacker who threatened to blow up a French airliner in protest at France's plans to resume nuclear testing in the South Pacific was not accountable for his act.
The jury agreed that the man, who might have been jailed for life for hijacking the Air Inter Airbus with 290 passengers and nine crew in September 1995, should be freed.
But it ordered that he should receive psychiatric treatment in Spain as an out-patient, the Swiss news agency ATS reported.

Two psychiatrists gave opposing opinions on the mental state of the man, an industrial designer from Palma de Mallorca identified by Spanish state radio as Carlos Santolaya, when he forced the Paris-bound flight to land at Geneva's Cointrin airport.

The jury appeared to be swayed by the view that he was temporarily mentally unstable when he stormed into the cockpit and threatened to detonate a bomb connected to what turned out to be a mobile phone taped with batteries, ATS said.
He said he had wanted to protest over France's plans at the time to resume nuclear testing at Murora in the South Pacific. He surrendered after releasing everyone on board.
